ambition.rationale: The core problem is a forensic reconstruction: a hand-written, time-dependent spread solver is inverted against sparse, late perimeters to estimate ignition place, start time and spread scale, with a calibrated 90% region and an identifiability gate. That is a hard inverse problem, not a familiar app with a model attached, and no named fire-spread engine is used. It stops short of 8 because the newest input is mainly the 2026 USGS inventory, and that is used to benchmark an ordinary random forest and MLP rather than to change the inversion. The weather and house-level inputs are older public sources, the house-level statistics are standard epidemiology, the analyst is a common tool-calling loop, and the app shell copies a public concept. The per-fit length-to-breadth cap is a fitted stand-in for spotting, so part of the hard physics is a correction rather than a mechanism.

depth.rationale:
Score 7.5 on depth of the hard part. The back end contains real original engineering. pipeline/ember/spread.py hand-implements an Anderson length-to-breadth ratio and an elliptical spread factor, and runs a time-dependent label-setting search with its own heap. pipeline/steps/s11_ignition.py runs a brute-force inverse search with a simulation-calibrated posterior temperature and an identifiability gate that withholds the start time. s09b hand-codes the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio with its RBG variance and an IRLS logistic fit. web/api/_lib/verify.ts grounds the analyst's numbers against the cited tool outputs. The spread physics and the stats formulas check out where I read them, and the start-time gate is load-bearing: both real fires withhold a start time.

The depth is weaker than the code suggests in four places. (1) Eaton's headline fit picks lb_max 1.0, which collapses spread to isotropic, and the Eaton synthetic benchmark draws its truths in [1.0, 1.25], so the elliptical physics is barely exercised for the fire the app leads with. (2) The synthetic truths are generated by the same spread function the inverter uses, and the start-time baseline is a weak area back-extrapolation. On Eaton the back-trace location loses to the first-footprint centroid on median error (588 m vs 449 m). (3) The debris models are stock sklearn estimators with fixed hyperparameters; the original part there is the evaluation harness (within-storm AUC, cluster bootstrap, monotone constraint). (4) The recalibrated M1 flips the sign of the burn-severity term, and that is explained only in model_eval.json notes.

Share, by my count of lines. Original algorithmic logic is about 1,600 lines: spread.py about 380, s11 about 360, s06 about 110, s09b about 120, debris.py about 100, analyst.ts about 120, verify.ts about 120, tools.ts about 220, geo.ts and names.ts about 80. Evaluation design around library models is about 440 lines: s14 about 240 and the eval-analyst truth and scoring about 200. Together that is about 2,040 of about 17,170 non-test app lines, or about 12% (about 24% of the non-UI back end). Glue is the rest: ETL steps s01 to s10 (about 3,000 lines), web/src (8,615 lines of UI and rendering), and report and format code. Counting ETL as pipeline would give about 29%; counting whole hard-part files gives about 27%. The advisor's 35 to 45 percent estimate is high on this count. No copied or vendored code was found; the only licence strings are data attributions.

judge.rationale:
Verdict: reject, on approval rule 1 alone. The fixed arithmetic gives 76.5 (weighted 76.5 + Meta bonus 0), below 80, before my verdict is consulted. Rule 2 holds: zero critical findings survived, and after checking all six adversary findings against the repository I agree none is critical (F2 and F5 are true wording errors, F1 is a taxonomy choice the manifest note discloses, F3, F4 and F6 are wording). One thing the arithmetic hides: the panel output has bonus: null, which means the Meta-bonus agent failed validation twice and was counted as 0 (docs/judge/judge-round.js:188), the same harness fault that zeroed two agents in round 1. Rounds 2-4 scored the bonus 2 with no live run; HEAD now commits live outputs for both Meta models (web/public/data/{eaton,palisades}/eval/analyst.json with per-question tool calls, pipeline/logs/smoke-meta.log for muse-spark-1.3 and sam-3.1, and web/api/_tests/model.test.ts driving the real OpenAI-SDK client over a recorded transport), so a scored bonus would plausibly be 2 to 3. Even at 3 the total is 79.5, so the reject stands on merit, but the true gap is about half a point in one 25%-weight dimension, not three and a half points. With my own scores substituted (depth 8, evidence 8, execution 7.5, the rest as the panel scored) the weighted score is 77.25.

What I verified myself, read-only on the judged checkout at 95f68fb and by running the documented commands from a fresh scratchpad copy with the runner's venv:

Where I read the panel differently (details in disagreements): depth is 8, not 7.5, because the panel's 12% share counts 8,615 lines of UI as glue, while the rubric's contrast is original logic versus a wrapper around one API call, and the spread solver, inversion, calibration, hand-coded statistics, grounding verifier and evaluation harness are all original and checked out where I read them.
